thread.title: Nasdaq logs worst day in 3 weeks as technology sector sinks stock market to start Thanksgiving week

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Nasdaq logs worst day in 3 weeks as technology sector sinks stock market to start Thanksgiving week
text:
The Nasdaq Composite Index on Monday logged the worst decline since late October and the S&P 500 and Dow suffered their worst day in about a week, as a fresh tumble in technology and internet-related shares dragged major benchmarks in the red. The Nasdaq COMP, -3.03% closed down 3% at 7,028--performing the worst among its benchmarks to commence a holiday-shortened week. The day's loss was the worst for the Nasdaq since Oct. 24, according to FactSet data. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.56% ended down 395 points, or 1.6%, at 25,017, while the S&P 500 index SPX, -1.66% declined 1.7% at 2,690. The fall for the S&P 500 and the Dow represented their worst since Nov. 12, according to FactSet data. That said, Monday's selloff came amid a lower volume period, with markets closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving. Shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, -3.96% dropped 4% and narrowly avoided a close in bear-market territory, defined as a decline from a recent peak of at least 20%, while shares of Google-parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -3.91% GOOGL, -3.82% ended in a bear market for the first time since around 2011, highlighting a deterioration in popular tech and growth names that had helped to drive the markets to repeated records but were now in sharp retreat. Monday's downturn accelerated as a report on home-builder confidence came in weaker than expected.
